### Jerusalem Captured
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/jerusalem-captured
Passage: 2 Kings 24:18–25:21
Points:
- Zedekiah persisted in idolatry and rebelled against Babylon by trusting earthly alliances rather than God.
- Following a brutal two-year siege, Jerusalem fell, leading to the execution of the royal heirs and the capture of the king.
- The Babylonians burnt the temple, dismantled its sacred bronze furnishings, and hauled its valuables away to Babylon.
- Only the poorest and least influential residents remained behind to work the land, while the rest were deported.
- Though the Lord is exceedingly patient, His judgment and discipline against persistent sin will not delay forever.

### Devotional: 2 Kings 25
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/2-kings-25-hebrews-7-amos-1-psalm-144/
Passage: 2 Kings 25
Points:
- Both Jeremiah and Ezekiel warned that God decreed Jerusalem's fall because the nation had abandoned Him.
- Zedekiah’s foolish rebellion brought devastating Babylonian retaliation, ending with his blinding and exile.
- Jerusalem was systematically destroyed: the temple and palaces were burned, walls pulled down, and sacred furnishings plundered.
- The mass of the populace was carried into exile, leaving only the poorest behind under an ill-fated governorship.
- The book concludes with a ray of hope when Jehoiachin is released from prison, proving the Davidic line is not extinguished.
